entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Smt Archana Tiwari - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Mayur Gulati - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/Sta
Heard on I.A. No.16621/2024 which is second application under Section 430(1) of Bnss, 2023 for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 08.07.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Niwas, District Mandla (M.P.) in S.T. No.19/2021, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363, 366(A) and 376 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 07 years with fine of Rs.2000/-; R.I. for 07 years with fine of Rs.2000/- and R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulations.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Niwas, District Mandla (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant has further been convicted under Section 3 r/w Section 4 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulation.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellant that the present appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He remained in custody for 04 years 07 months and 18 days.
DNA report is negative and FIR is also lodged after a period of 24 hours but no plausible explanation has been offered by the prosecutrix or the prosecution.

It is also submitted that though prosecutrix stick to the statement given by her but 2 CRA-11470-2023 keeping in view the contradictions and omissions reflected from the cross- examination of the witnesses, he has a good case on merits.
He is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
It is also submitted that the present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal.
The appellant has no criminal antecedents.
It is prayed that the benefit of suspension of sentence be granted and the appellant be released on bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer made by the appellant on the ground that there was injury found on the private part of the prosecutrix by Dr.
Malti Uikey (PW-11) and it is also reflected from the statement of prosecutrix that after tearing the cloths of prosecutrix, forceful rape has been committed by the present appellant.
The age of the prosecutrix at the time of commission of offence was 16 years, 07 months and 17 days.
Though DNA report is negative but keeping in view the statement of prosecutrix which are supported by medical evidence, no ground for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is made out.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Considering the rival contentions of the parties, evidence available on record and having regard to the attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that this is not a fit case for suspension of sentence at this stage.
Accordingly, I.A. No.16621/2024 is dismissed.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE 3 CRA-11470-2023 DV Sandeep Maravi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54739905/
